name: Hawaii hotspot
note: The Pacific plate slides north-west over a plume of hot mantle, leaving a line of volcanoes: the Hawaiian–Emperor chain. The bend, about 47 million years old, shows where the plate's motion changed.
facts: Kīlauea, Mauna Loa, and Kamaʻehuakanaloa offshore

name: Yellowstone hotspot
note: Under Yellowstone National Park. As North America moved west over it, it left a trail of huge calderas across Idaho's Snake River Plain.
facts: Old Faithful and over 10,000 hot springs and geysers

name: Iceland hotspot
note: A plume under the Mid-Atlantic Ridge: the extra magma built Iceland, the largest island on a spreading ridge.

name: Réunion hotspot
note: Today under Réunion's Piton de la Fournaise. About 66 million years ago, with India above it, it poured out the Deccan Traps, one of the largest lava floods in Earth's history.
facts: Mauritius, the Chagos, the Maldives, the Laccadives, the Deccan Traps

name: Galápagos hotspot
note: Under the Galápagos Islands, whose volcanoes are among the most active on Earth. The islands' different ages helped Darwin see how species change.
facts: The Carnegie Ridge and the Cocos Ridge

name: Tristan hotspot
note: Under Tristan da Cunha. When the South Atlantic opened about 132 million years ago it made the Etendeka lavas of Namibia, and its trail is the Walvis Ridge.
facts: The Walvis Ridge and the Rio Grande Rise

name: Afar plume
note: Under the Afar Triangle in Ethiopia and Djibouti, where the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden and the East African Rift meet: one of the hottest and lowest places on land.
facts: Erta Ale's lava lake, and Danakil's salt flats

name: Azores hotspot
note: Near where the North American, Eurasian and African plates meet, building the Azores islands.

name: Canary hotspot
note: Built the Canary Islands, oldest in the east (Fuerteventura) and youngest in the west (El Hierro). La Palma erupted in 2021.

name: Easter hotspot
note: Near the East Pacific Rise; it built Easter Island (Rapa Nui).

name: Samoa hotspot
note: Built the Samoan Islands; Vailuluʻu, an active undersea volcano, sits over it.

name: Louisville hotspot
note: Its trail, the Louisville Seamount Chain, is the southern twin of the Hawaiian–Emperor chain.

name: Kerguelen hotspot
note: It built the Kerguelen Plateau, one of the largest volcanic plateaus on Earth, mostly under the sea.

name: Cape Verde hotspot
note: Built the Cape Verde Islands; Fogo is its active volcano.

name: Macdonald hotspot
note: Under the Macdonald Seamount, an active undersea volcano south of French Polynesia; its trail includes the Austral Islands.

name: Eifel hotspot
note: Under western Germany; its maars (crater lakes) are about 11,000 years old.
